claims.text: Unprocessed red meat intake is not associated with incident coronary heart disease.
Unprocessed red meat intake is not associated with incident diabetes mellitus.
Processed meat intake is associated with a 42% higher risk of incident coronary heart disease per 50-g serving per day.
Processed meat intake is associated with a 19% higher risk of incident diabetes mellitus per 50-g serving per day.
Unprocessed red meat consumption is not associated with incident stroke.
Processed meat consumption is not associated with incident stroke.

evidence.description: Red meat intake was not associated with CHD (n=4 studies; relative risk per 100-g serving per day=1.00; 95% confidence interval, 0.81 to 1.23; P for heterogeneity=0.36).
Red meat intake was not associated with diabetes mellitus (n=5; relative risk=1.16; 95% confidence interval, 0.92 to 1.46; P=0.25).
Processed meat intake was associated with 42% higher risk of CHD (n=5; relative risk per 50-g serving per day=1.42; 95% confidence interval, 1.07 to 1.89; P=0.04).
Processed meat intake was associated with 19% higher risk of diabetes mellitus (n=7; relative risk=1.19; 95% confidence interval, 1.11 to 1.27; P<0.001).
Consumption of red and processed meat were not associated with stroke, but only 3 studies evaluated these relationships.
Consumption of red and processed meat were not associated with stroke, but only 3 studies evaluated these relationships.

methodologies.name: Systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis
methodologies.description: Systematic review and meta-analysis using random-effects generalized least squares models to derive pooled dose-response estimates across prospective cohort and case-control studies.

limitations.text: Meat consumption is inconsistently associated with development of CHD, stroke, and diabetes mellitus in prior literature, limiting quantitative recommendations for consumption levels.
Only 3 identified studies evaluated the relationships of red and processed meat consumption with incident stroke.

future_work.text: Better understanding of potential mechanisms of effects of processed versus red meats on health outcomes.
